issue: Is a district court order disentitling a foreign defendant who has remained abroad, without evasion or concealment, immediately appealable under the collateral order doctrine?

sides.position: An order disentitling a foreign citizen who has remained at home abroad, without evasion, stealth, or concealment, is immediately appealable under the collateral order doctrine.
cases: United States v. Sindzingre, 7 F.4th 127 (2d Cir. 2021)

sides.position: Fugitive disentitlement orders, including those involving a foreign citizen located abroad, are not immediately appealable.
cases: United States v. Shalhoub, 855 F.3d 1255 (11th Cir. 2017)
United States v. Martirossian, 917 F.3d at 887

this_court: The majority holds the order is immediately appealable and this Court has jurisdiction. The dissent would hold the Court lacks appellate jurisdiction.
quote: In doing so, it creates a split with our sister circuits who have held fugitive disentitlement orders—and specifically involving, as here, a foreign citizen located abroad—are not immediately appealable.
cite: United States v. Sindzingre, 7 F.4th 127 (2d Cir. 2021)
